messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on multi-GPU KV-path after the kernel-selector revert. 8xA100, tp=2 pp=4, steady-state token latency is ~18% higher for long-context streams (8k tokens).
jonathan: Hmm, same here on our canary. Nightly microbench shows throughput drop ~14% for streaming profiles. Did you get profiles? :eyes:
perf-bot: nightly-run-2026-03-17: tp=2 pp=4 8xA100 | model=xlarge-v2 | throughput -14% | latency +18% | diff-artifact: https://ci.redwood/artefacts/1845678901 (flame/alloc) :warning:
maria: Pasted the flame + alloc trace: the hot spot is in kvcache sync paths — lots of time in all-reduce and memcpy during past-key fetch + kernel selection calls. Also seeing increased number of small all-reduces per step.
lee: Can you paste the bench command and the kernel-selection logs? Curious whether the selector chose different matmul kernels post-revert.
maria: Sure — here's the run command we used:
```
python infra/bench/stream_bench.py --model xlarge-v2 --gpus 8 --tp 2 --pp 4 --sequence 8192 \
  --kvcache-strategy stripe --batching heuristic --warmup 1000 --steps 500
```
and here's the kernel selector snapshot (snippet):
```
layer_14: chosen_kernel=matmul_warp32_f32
layer_15: chosen_kernel=matmul_warp16_f32
layer_16: chosen_kernel=matmul_warp32_f32  # previously warp16
...
```
jonathan: Interesting — mixed kernel choices per layer could increase kernel launch overhead and prevent stream reuse. But flame shows majority time locked in NCCL/all-reduce waits. I'm leaning toward this being a kvcache sharding + sync-frequency issue rather than pure kernel perf.
sara: Quick primer — our kvcache modes: replicate (DP-like) = low-latency local reads, high memory; stripe-by-layer (PP affinity) = each gpu owns subset of layers' KV, needs RPC/all-reduce for cross-layer lookups; stripe-by-token (TP affinity) = shards within TP groups, reduces cross-pp traffic but needs per-step all-reduce across TP groups. Each has tradeoffs with TP/PP/DP geometry.
lee: From the profile: all-reduce latency per step jumped from ~6ms -> ~38ms for kvcache syncs. That's consistent with a switch from delta-compress to full-sync path in the revert. Any logs about compression being disabled?
maria: Yes — kernel-selector revert also removed the delta-encode path because it relied on a new tensor-compress kernel that got rolled back. So we're falling back to full NCCL all-reduce of KV deltas.
jonathan: That explains the throughput hit. Fix options: (1) Re-enable delta-compress kernel (needs recreate + QA), (2) change default kvcache strategy to lazy fetch + on-demand RPC (reduce frequency), (3) change sharding: move to PP-local sharding so fewer cross-pp all-reduces, (4) optimize kernel selection to prefer uniform kernel shapes to reuse streams.
sara: Quick cost/latency tradeoffs: replicate (DP) removes all-reduce entirely but memory scales O(N) — with xlarge-v2 memory we'd blow per-GPU RAM on 8k context. PP-local sharding reduces cross-pp traffic but requires extra prefix fetch RPCs when a requested layer isn't local; with tp=2 pp=4 geometry it might cut the all-reduce participants by half.
maria: I ran a micro-experiment toggling kvcache mapping:
A) replicate -> latency +2% but memory +3x (not feasible)
B) pp-local (layer affinity) -> latency +6% but all-reduce time down 60%
C) tp-shard (within tp groups) -> latency +9% and all-reduce time down 40% but more small NCCL ops
Numbers are rough from 50-step runs.
lee: Sounds like B is best short-term. Also we should reduce sync frequency: switch sync to lazy-evict with batched all-reduce every K steps (K=4) — will amortize overhead for streaming workloads. Any spike in stale-kv correctness?
maria: For streaming we can tolerate slight staleness on past keys (we're not updating keys after generation), so batching syncs is safe. Tests with K=4 gave similar perplexity on eval prompts.
jonathan: Next steps I propose:
- sara: spell out memory cost for replicate for all target models (quick table)
- lee: add instrumentation to count NCCL ops and bytes per step and classify small vs large all-reduces
- maria: run A/B tests on prod-like infra with pp-local sharding + lazy-sync (K=4) and collect latency + tail percentiles
- sara: coordinate with infra to requeue delta-compress kernel rework as medium-priority if short-term fixes not sufficient

sara: I'll handle the memory calc and file a short doc.
maria: I'll start the A/B tonight and post results in this thread. If we see tail regressions we rollback to previous kvcache config.
lee: I'll add counters and a small flame harness to separate kernel-launch overhead from NCCL stalls. Expect logs by EOD.
jonathan: If we can get all-reduce bytes down via K-step batching + PP-local mapping we should recover most of the 14% throughput loss.
maria: Cool. Thanks all. Posting perf traces here as they come. :thumbsup:
